title: perf(service-messaging): index the inbox feed receipt window read by user, channel and created_at
body:
repo:objectstack#7 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibvVRcFWKrfWeG5jzPb

Part of #35530

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

This PR ships the receipt half of the card. The inbox half stays with the card, deferred for the reason under Acceptance notes.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：用户无感；铃铛每十秒读取的已读状态，在历史记录多的账号上不再随数据量变慢，实测从约二到三毫秒降到约零点一毫秒。
- 为什么做：属于页面加载提速的后续收尾；收件箱消息那一半暂缓，因为老的 MySQL 部署里那一列存成长文本，建不了索引。
- 出错会怎样：只影响查询速度，不改数据，可以直接撤回。
- 要你做什么：无。

## What changes

- `sys_notification_receipt` declares a third index, `(user_id, channel, created_at)`, beside `(notification_id, user_id, channel)` (unique, global) and `(user_id, state)`.
- New pin `src/objects/inbox-feed-window-indexes.integration.test.ts`, 3 tests. It pins the declaration on the built value, then runs a real `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3). On that engine, schema sync creates the index, and the SQL the engine actually emits for the bell's receipt read (captured off the connection) gets a SQLite plan that SEARCHes the new index and has no full `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY`.
- Changeset `.changeset/35530-inbox-window-indexes.md` (`patch`).
- `sys_inbox_message` is unchanged; its object file is byte-identical to `main`.

## Why

The Console bell polls `sys_notification_receipt` filtered by `user_id` + `channel: 'inbox'` every 10 s, newest first, top 20. The engine sends `order by created_at desc, id desc limit 20`. The table had no key that leads on the filter columns and continues with `created_at`, so the read searched `(user_id, state)` and then sorted the user's whole receipt range on every poll.

## Tests

Measured on a real `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3, in memory), on this branch's tree. The table holds 56,000 receipts. The measured user has 5,000 `inbox` and 5,000 `email` receipts spread across the timeline. A "quiet" user has 3,000 of each, all older than everyone else's. Each figure is the mean of 300 runs of the statement the engine emitted, after `ANALYZE`. Before-figures are given as a range where two runs differed.

| user | before (plan · ms) | after (plan · ms) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| spread | `SEARCH … USING INDEX idx_sys_notification_receipt_user_id_state (user_id=?)` + `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY` · 3.0 to 3.1 | `SEARCH … USING INDEX idx_sys_notification_receipt_user_id_channel_created_at (user_id=? AND channel=?)` + `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR LAST TERM OF ORDER BY` · 0.10 |
| quiet | same · 1.8 to 2.3 | same · 0.10 to 0.11 |

`FOR LAST TERM OF ORDER BY` sorts only rows that share a `created_at` (the driver's `id` tie-breaker), and the read stops at the window. A four-column variant ending in `id` measured the same within noise, and it would make `check:keyed-text-bounds` ask for a bound on the builtin `id` field.

## Acceptance notes

- **Deferred: the inbox half of the card, `(user_id, created_at)` on `sys_inbox_message`.** That index would key `sys_inbox_message.user_id`. The field has never declared a bound, so on an existing MySQL table it is `TEXT`, which MySQL refuses to index. Schema sync never rewrites a column type, and no drift op converts `TEXT` to `varchar`, because `narrow_varchar` requires a physical character column. Traced on main, the refusal travels like this:
  - `sql-driver-schema-sync.ts` sees MySQL refuse the `TEXT` key part, and for a plain index logs it and rethrows;
  - `sql-driver-managed-drift.ts` (`syncTableIndexes`) and `sql-driver-rotation.ts` (`initObjects`) pass it up uncaught;
  - the per-object loop in `@objectstack/objectql`'s plugin `syncRegisteredSchemas` catches it and logs it as a failed object.

  The boot survives and the object stays registered and served. The cost is a new `Schema sync FAILED` error on every boot of every existing MySQL deployment. It also skips that object's later per-boot steps: the drift reconcile, the canonical datetime/time/json/boolean backfills, and the MySQL datetime/time column migrations. The inbox index can land once the SQL driver either converges a keyed `TEXT` column to its declared `varchar(n)`, or refuses a plain non-unique index without throwing away the object's remaining steps.
- **Protocol and Clause-②.** Nothing a metadata author can write changes. `packages/spec` is untouched, `indexes` is an existing key, the object is a platform-shipped system object, no generated baseline or snapshot moves, and no accepted set narrows.
- **MySQL, receipt side.** Receipt tables created since the receipt columns declared their bounds already hold `user_id`/`channel` as `varchar`, so the new index builds. On an older receipt table, the existing `(user_id, state)` index is already refused before the new one is reached, so nothing changes there. This is read from the code: MySQL was not measured, and neither was PostgreSQL.
